The difference we make

What we do

Chasing the Stigma is a national mental health charity on a mission to normalise and humanise conversations about mental health, while ensuring that everyone in the UK can access clear pathways to support, whenever and wherever they need it.

We want to create a society where there is no longer a stigma associated with mental health, where people are as comfortable talking about their mental health as their physical health, and where everyone is able to find appropriate support before they reach a point of crisis, leading to a significant long-term reduction in self-harm and suicide.

​

We aim to achieve this through: 
 

  • Our pioneering Ambassador of Hope mental health training services

  • Awareness-raising campaigns and lobbying activities

  • The provision of the UK’s largest and most comprehensive directory of community mental health services, the Hub of Hope.

20K+ Given mental health training

We delivered our Ambassador of Hope training to over 20,000 individuals across the UK alone, equipping them to with the tools and knowledge to effectively signpost those who need support and help anyone dealing with a mental health crisis

The Hub of Hope lists over 14,000 services that are regularly monitored following guidance from our quality assurance documents, making it the UK's biggest and most comprehensive mental health service finder

14.5K Services listed on the Hub of Hope

We help 300,000 users to find and access mental health support through the Hub of Hope every year, averaging more than 25,700 active users every month.

300K+ People suported every year

With over a million searches for help a year, we're giving more options of hope to people than ever before and ensuring the pathway to mental health support is clear

1M+ Searches for support

With lived experience
at our core

Chasing the Stigma was established by CEO and founder, Jake Mills, following his own battle with depression and suicide attempt in 2013.

 

During his recovery, Jake went public about his mental health issues, speaking out on social media and to regional and national media. As he did, he was flooded with messages from people who were also struggling and who - like himself - found nowhere to turn for help.

 

Discovering this lack of clear signposting to local and relevant support, and determined to ensure people could find the help they needed when they needed it, Jake began building a centralised database of mental health services. That database became the Hub of Hope, now the UK’s largest and most comprehensive directory of community mental health services, listing tens of thousands of services for the 300,000+ people who use it each year.

 

Jake continues to advocate for people with lived experience of mental health issues in the corridors of power, speaking to government, politicians and leaders in the statutory and voluntary sector to drive change in response to mental health. Through his leadership he also highlights the importance of acknowledging that we all have mental health, and empowers people to look after their own, and recognise and support it in others

We aim to humanise and normalise mental health, actively challenge the stigma associated with mental illness and remove the barriers that prevent people from seeking help.

​

​Almost three quarters of those who die by suicide each year are not known to mental health services or have not been seen within a year previous to their death. Quite simply, people are dying without accessing the help or support they so desperately need, and we want to change this.

​

​Our vision is to make help as easy as possible to find while creating true environments of understanding across the UK, revolutionising the UK’s approach to Mental Health.
 

If this resonates with you, contact us and let’s talk!
